newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures close higher across board.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures close higher across board.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was quiet at midday on Monday with holidays in Japan and Thailand keeping most of the trade on the sidelines, but prices were marked up slightly in the afternoon session on some speculative buying interest, dealers said.
Very few people are back. The long stretch of holidays affected trading in the morning, they said.
News of the end of the nearly three week-long strike in Goodyear Tire was greeted cautiously by dealers.
"I think the workers still have to ratify the agreement so we have to see how that situation works out," a trader said.
The Thai government's decision to increase its support price for RSS3 grade rubber was ignored by the market, dealers said.
At around 0945 GMT, September RSS3 rose 1.50 cents 110.25 U.S. cents a kg.
June RSS1 rose 1.50 cents to 157.00 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg.
July TSR20 rose 1.50 cents to 151.50 Singapore cents (US$1.05) a kg.
